Paraphrasing
Week 5.1

What is paraphrasing?
• Paraphrasing is the act of restating someone else's words or ideas using
your own words while maintaining the original meaning.
• It involves expressing the information from a source in a different way,
often with a different sentence structure and vocabulary, while still
conveying the same key points or concepts.
• When paraphrasing, it is essential to accurately represent the original
meaning while using different language.

Example of Paraphrasing
Original Text: People tend to assume that developed nations have cleaner seas.
Paraphrased Text:
- Everyone seems to believe that the oceans of industrialized countries are more pristine.
- It is common knowledge that people think advanced countries contain oceans that are cleaner
than countries that are less advanced.
-Normally, people make the assumption that seas in nations that are more flourished are
cleaner.

Noun Clause
Original Text:
Noun Clause: Her singing is something she enjoys whenever she is in a happy mood
Paraphrased Text:
Adjective Clause: She is someone who likes to sing when her mood is happy.
Adverb Clause: When she is in a delightful mood, she loves to sing.

Many Possible Outcomes
There are many possible ways to paraphrase. As long as you make sure that the sentence you rewrote has the same meaning as
the original text and still makes sense.
Original Text: He is the man who stole my wallet. He must be punished.
(noun) (adjective clause)
Paraphrased Text:
Compound Sentence: That is the gentleman who nabbed my wallet, so there needs to be some form of punishment for him.
Adverb Clause: Because this man robbed me of my wallet, he needs to be penalized in some way.
Noun Clause: What this man did to deserve punishment was steal my wallet.

Active & Passive Voice
Active Voice:
The subject of a sentence takes
action, usually by performing an
action or making a statement.
Example: She is reading a book.
Passive Voice:
The subject of a sentence receives
the action instead of performing
it.
Example: The book is read by her.

ACTIVE VOICE
I kicked the ball.
PASSIVE VOICE
The ball was
kicked (by me).

Passive
voice is the
opposite
of active
voice.
• Active: Everybody loves chocolate.
• Passive: Chocolate is loved by everybody.
• Active: The lifeguard saved a man.
• Passive: A man was saved by the lifeguard.
• Active: Decorators are painting my house.
• Passive: My house is being painted by
decorators.

Why Do We
Use Passive?
Reason #1
When the action is more important or interesting than the person/thing who
does the action.
Passive: $100,000 were donated to charity.
(Who donated it? Not important. I am more impressed with the money.)
Active: Bill Gates donated $100,000 to charity.
(Wow, the person who did the action was more interesting than the action)

Why Do We
Use Passive?
Reason #2
The person who does the action is not known, or not important.
Passive: This beautiful bridge was built in 1732.
(Who built the bridge? I don’t know. Or, not important to me.)
Active: John Taylor Thomas built the bridge in 1732.
(He is famous, so I know him. He is important for a certain situation)

Why Do We
Use Passive?
Reason #3
The person doing the action is obvious.
Passive: Billy was arrested last night!
(Who arrested Billy? The police, duh! Do you think the mailman did it?)
Active: The police arrested Bill last night.

Why Do We
Use Passive?
Reason #4
The object cannot do the action itself.
Passive: 100 chocolate cakes were sold on Sunday.
(Can the cake sell itself? No way. Only a person can sell cake. Since
the person is not important, they are not mentioned)

What is
an agent?

When you
want to say
WHO does the
action; use an
agent.
When using an agent in passive voice = By + person (this is optional)
$100,000 were donated to charity by Bill Gates.
This beautiful bridge was built in 1732 by John Taylor Thomas.
100 chocolate cakes were sold on Sunday by Little Home Bakery.

Extra Notes
Please keep in mind that every sentence example shown in these slides are examples that show possible
ways to paraphrase.
There is more than just the methods on these slides for paraphrasing text.
The examples here are just to help you get started and to have an idea of how you should be
paraphrasing.
Just be sure that whatever you paraphrase, the text keeps the same meaning as the original text.

Common Mistake Students Have Made in the
Past
Changing the tense of a sentence is not paraphrasing:
I am walking to the bus station.
I was walking to the bus station.

Common Mistake Students Have Made in the
Past
Adding information that is not from the original text is not paraphrasing:
Original Text:
In August 2015, the new CD “Elvis Presley Forever” debuted at No. 1 on Billboard’s
Top Rock Albums chart.
Paraphrased Text:
The new CD “Elvis Presley Forever” that everyone bought was ranked No. 1 on
Billboard’s Top Rock Albums chart in August 2015 because everyone liked it.
